title: Min Stack Operation Sequence
hints: getMin needs to be fast every time, not just scan-the-stack fast - what if you tracked the running minimum alongside every push?
keep a second stack that mirrors the first: each time you push a value, also push the minimum-so-far (min of the new value and whatever was the previous minimum) onto this second stack
when you pop from the main stack, pop from the min-tracking stack too, so it always reflects the minimum of exactly what's currently on the main stack
getMin then just peeks the top of the min-tracking stack, no scanning needed
commonMistakes: tracking a single running minimum variable instead of a stack of minimums, which breaks once you pop past the value that was the minimum
not keeping the min-tracking stack in lockstep with every push and pop on the main stack
parsing 'push_-2' incorrectly by splitting on every underscore or dash instead of just the first underscore

content.problemStatement:
You're given a space-delimited sequence of `ops` to run against a stack
that also supports finding its current minimum. Each token is one of:

- `"push_<value>"` - push the integer value onto the stack
- `"pop"` - remove the top element
- `"top"` - peek at the top element (no return value needed)
- `"getMin"` - report the current minimum value in the stack

**Simulate the operations in order on an initially empty stack, and return a list containing the result of every "getMin" operation, in the order they occurred.**

You can assume `"pop"`, `"top"`, and `"getMin"` are never called on an
empty stack.
constraints: pop, top, and getMin are never called on an empty stack
notes: the current minimum is pushed multiple times, then popped once (minimum should not disappear early)
getMin called immediately after the very first push
a long run of pushes with a strictly decreasing sequence of minimums

sampleTestCases.input: ops = "push_-2 push_0 push_-3 getMin pop getMin"
sampleTestCases.explanation: stack becomes [-2,0,-3], getMin reports -3; pop removes -3 -> [-2,0]; getMin reports -2

sampleTestCases.input: ops = "push_5 push_3 getMin push_1 getMin pop getMin"
sampleTestCases.explanation: [5,3] getMin=3; push 1 -> [5,3,1] getMin=1; pop removes 1 -> [5,3] getMin=3

sampleTestCases.input: ops = "push_1 push_1 push_1 getMin pop getMin"
sampleTestCases.explanation: duplicate minimums must still be tracked correctly after a pop

optimal.pattern: stack augmented with a parallel min-tracking stack

bruteForce.approach: use a plain stack for values, and for every getMin call scan the entire stack to find the minimum
bruteForce.time: O(n) per getMin call, O(n^2) overall in the worst case
